# PowerOperatorCanBeUsed

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" /> <Badge type="tip" text="quick-fix" /> <Badge type="info" text="PHP ≥ 5.6" />

Group: [Language level migration](/rules/#language-level-migration) · PhpStorm name: `PowerOperatorCanBeUsedInspection`

Since PHP 5.6 exponentiation has its own operator. `pow($a, $b)` can be
written `$a ** $b`, which is shorter and avoids a function call.

## Example

::: code-group

```php{2,3,4,5,6} [Before]
<?php
$area   = pow($side, 2);
$growth = pow($rate * 0.01 + 1, $years);
$scaled = \pow(2, $bits - 1);
$total  = $offset - pow($k, $m);
$safe   = pow($q ?? 0, $flag ? 2 : 3);
$keep   = pow($side);
$meth   = $calc->pow($side, 2);
```

```php [After fix]
<?php
$area   = $side ** 2;
$growth = ($rate * 0.01 + 1) ** $years;
$scaled = 2 ** ($bits - 1);
$total  = $offset - ($k ** $m);
$safe   = ($q ?? 0) ** ($flag ? 2 : 3);
$keep   = pow($side);
$meth   = $calc->pow($side, 2);
```

:::

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Use &#39;$side ** 2&#39; (exponentiation operator) instead.</li>
<li>line 3: Use &#39;($rate * 0.01 + 1) ** $years&#39; (exponentiation operator) instead.</li>
<li>line 4: Use &#39;2 ** ($bits - 1)&#39; (exponentiation operator) instead.</li>
<li>line 5: Use &#39;($k ** $m)&#39; (exponentiation operator) instead.</li>
<li>line 6: Use &#39;($q ?? 0) ** ($flag ? 2 : 3)&#39; (exponentiation operator) instead.</li>
</ul>

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "PowerOperatorCanBeUsed": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file), either of:

```php
// @custos-ignore PowerOperatorCanBeUsed

/**
 * @noinspection PowerOperatorCanBeUsedInspection
 */
```
